chunks: And from him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd, from Abū Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام informed me and said: The deceased is begun with at his private part, then wudu (ablution) is performed for him like the wudu of salat (prayer), and he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), used here to specify the manner of the wudu
key_terms.الْحَدِيثَ: the hadith or report, indicating the narration continues beyond this excerpt
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person whose funeral washing is being discussed
key_terms.بِفَرْجِهِ: with his private part; indicating the initial step of cleansing

ai.seo_question: What is the order of wudu (ablution) and preparation before performing ghusl for a deceased person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the order of preparation for washing the deceased, beginning with cleaning the private part and then performing wudu (ablution) like the wudu of salat (prayer). It is a jurisprudential report related to the rites of taharah and the treatment of the dead before ghusl.
